subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "holds the funds"
reading: A reading: the holder role is CM-PAY-004's (the processors, acquirers and licensed entities that hold the merchant's funds behind the platform's service), where Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce answer (processors, Financial Services Providers, Global-e, Stripe, PayPal). Salla, Zid, WooPayments and BigCommerce Payments also answer with the service's balance, CM-PAY-005's thing; BigCommerce's standalone PayPal gateway and merchant service provider with CM-PAY-011; and cash on delivery (Salla's COD balance, Zid Ship) with CM-PAY-029. Held per market through the market's setting (S01-E1), so capability.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "settlement of funds"
reading: A reading: settling to the merchant is CM-PAY-004's thing (the entities that process and settle the service's transactions), where Shopify (Payment Processor, acquirer), WooCommerce (Stripe, Network International) and BigCommerce (the PayPal platform account, S01-BC-069) answer. Salla's "a Salla service ... settling transactions with banks" (S01-SA-139) and BigCommerce Payments' account (S01-BC-070) name the service itself, CM-PAY-002's; Zid Pay crediting the balance (S01-ZD-023) and Shopify's Managed Markets settlement through the Shopify Payments account (S01-SH-141) are CM-PAY-005's; Stripe, BitPay and other gateways on BigCommerce are CM-PAY-011's; Tamara on Salla is CM-PAY-015's; the carrier or Zid Ship for cash on delivery is CM-PAY-029's.
conflict: placement (rows: S01-D2, model): on Salla, S01-SA-104 (V-037, scope تمارا) says "تتم تسوية كافة المدفوعات من قبل تمارا", a third party settling the merchant's instalment payments, while the CM-PAY-015 Salla cell is core only (SA-C-118/where/SA-S-0070, the plan line SA-C-118/decides/SA-S-1965, the released flags) and places no party outside; Tamara is among its slot fillers but placed nowhere. Zid's cell places the like statement outside (ZD-C-013/responsible/ZD-S-0625, Tabby pays the stores directly). A reading: the statement bears out an outside placement beside core on Salla; S01-D2's answer (each provider settles on its own terms) agrees with the subject's side.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "payouts"

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "collect payment"
reading: A reading: collecting and processing the buyer's payment behind the platform's service is CM-PAY-004's thing, where Shopify (third-party processors, the Payment Processor List), WooCommerce (Stripe), Zid (مقدمي خدمات الدفع) and BigCommerce (PayPal behind BigCommerce Payments) answer; Salla's "خدمة تقدمها سلة لمعالجة المدفوعات" (SA-S-0049) and BigCommerce Payments name the service itself, CM-PAY-002's. Other answers sit in each flow's capability: connected gateways (CM-PAY-011), stc pay through Salla's gateway (CM-PAY-012), Tabby (CM-PAY-015), the Zid Cashier payment device (CM-PAY-021), carriers, the merchant's courier and Zid Ship for cash on delivery (CM-PAY-029), and Trendyol and Jahez through Mazeed on Zid (CM-CHN-003).
conflict: placement (rows: S01-D4, model): on Salla, S01-SA-101 (V-088, "تُحصّل المدفوعات التي تتم عبر تابي من خلال تابي وليس من خلال مدفوعات سلة") shows Tabby collecting the buyer's payment, while the CM-PAY-015 Salla cell is core only (SA-C-118/where/SA-S-0070, SA-C-118/decides/SA-S-1965) with no party placed outside; Zid's cell places Tabby outside (ZD-C-013/responsible/ZD-S-0625). A reading: the statement bears out an outside placement beside core; S01-D4 (each provider collects) agrees with the subject's side. The same cell as in S01-VP-02, S01-VP-03 and S01-VP-09.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "pay you directly"
reading: A reading: the buyer paying the merchant directly, outside any payment service, is CM-PAY-016's thing (manual payment methods: Shopify's, WooCommerce's cheque, BigCommerce's offline methods), with bank transfer to the merchant's own account in CM-PAY-030 (Salla, WooCommerce's BACS, Zid, BigCommerce's Bank Deposit) and Shopify's on-chain transfers in CM-PAY-018. The merchant receives; the platform provides the method.
conflict: count (rows: S01-VP-05, model): the subject's BigCommerce statements S01-BC-115 to S01-BC-119 (V-111, V-621, V-622), from BigCommerce's help page Configuring Offline Payment Methods, say the merchant sets up in its store a Bank Deposit, Cash on Delivery, Check, Money Order or Pay in Store payment method ("You can set up your store to allow your customers to make a payment directly into your bank account by setting up a Bank Deposit payment method"): BigCommerce's own setting, which places it core by B-extent's rule. The CM-PAY-016 BigCommerce cell is not-stated (BC-C-022/boundary/BC-S-0129, shows, whose reading says the Help Center page on offline payment methods isn't held), and the CM-PAY-030 BigCommerce cell is none-held. A reading: the statements bear out core on both; S01-VP-05's commonality rests on the subject's side.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "agent"
reading: A reading: the agent role is a party standing for the merchant toward the processors and in receiving funds, CM-PAY-004's thing (Shopify as agent delivering instructions to the Payment Processors, SH-S-0079; Stripe, SPC, Network International and Stripe Japan as WooPayments users' agents). Zid's authorization to execute each payment on the merchant's behalf is cited in CM-PAY-020 (ZD-S-0543), and Salla's authorization to use the merchant's connected charity gateway account is CM-PAY-011's.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "Reserve"
reading: A reading: reserves are CM-PAY-006's thing by name (Shopify Reserves, Reserve Account), where Shopify (Shopify, Stripe, the processor), WooCommerce (Stripe, SPC, Network International) and Zid (Zid Pay) answer; Salla's and BigCommerce's only variants are gaps.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "withhold"
reading: A reading: holding back the merchant's funds from its payouts is CM-PAY-006's thing (reserves and payout holds), where Shopify, WooCommerce and Zid answer. Salla's delay of transfers under the Saudi Central Bank's restrictions (S01-SA-089) is a delay of the balance's payout, CM-PAY-005's, and its dashboard's share of payments held by the issuing bank for disputes (S01-SA-180, S01-SA-181) is CM-PAY-009's.
conflict: placement (rows: S01-VP-08, model): on Salla, the dashboard strings S01-SA-180 and S01-SA-181 (V-546, "Percentage of payments held by the issuing bank due to disputes during the selected period") show the card's issuing bank, a third party, holding disputed payments, while the CM-PAY-009 Salla cell is core only (SA-C-122/responsible/SA-S-5051) and lists no issuer among its slot fillers; Shopify's cell places the cardholder's bank outside (SH-C-072/decides/SH-S-0395, SH-C-072/decides/SH-S-0396). A reading: the strings bear out an outside placement beside core, and also give Salla's cell a dashboard statement in a term its search lists (اعتراضات), which the cell doesn't hold.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "deduct"
reading: A reading: deducting fees, refunds and amounts owed from what the merchant is paid is done on the service's balance, CM-PAY-005's thing, where Shopify, WooPayments and Zid Pay answer (and Zid's Mazeed share, ZD-S-0705). Stripe deducting from the Stripe account balance and the acquirer debiting the payout account are CM-PAY-004's; Tamara on Salla is CM-PAY-015's; Zid's deduction from the merchant wallet (محفظة التاجر) is CM-PLN-006's; Trendyol and Amazon deducting their fees on Zid are the channel's, CM-CHN-003.
conflict: placement (rows: S01-D6, model): on Salla, S01-SA-106 (V-165, scope تمارا, "يتم خصم المبلغ مباشرة من تمارا وليس من رصيد مدفوعات سلة") shows a refund on a Tamara order taken from Tamara, a third party, and not from Salla's balance, while the CM-PAY-015 Salla cell is core only (SA-C-118/where/SA-S-0070) with no party placed outside. A reading: the statement bears out an outside placement beside core; S01-D6 (each provider deducts its own) agrees with the subject's side. The same cell as in S01-VP-02, S01-VP-03 and S01-VP-04.

subject: S-01
question: who or what fills "security interest"
reading: A reading: a lien or security interest on the funds processed is held where the funds are, CM-PAY-004's thing, whose Shopify cell cites Shopify's lien (SH-S-0111, shows); WooCommerce's answers (SPC, Stripe's lien) are Stripe's terms, behind WooPayments. Salla's, Zid's and BigCommerce's only variants are gaps.
